description: Finnish passenger car (M1) periodic inspection (määräaikaiskatsastus) results for inspection year 2025, by make, model series and first registration year, with national averages by age and powertrain and the most common rejection causes. All numbers are Traficom official statistics unless a field says otherwise.

fieldNotes.firstRegYear: Käyttöönottovuosi: year the car was first taken into use (first registration, in Finland or abroad).
fieldNotes.ageYears: 2025 minus firstRegYear (approximate age at the 2025 inspection). Not a Traficom field.
fieldNotes.inspections: Number of periodic inspections (katsastustapahtumat) in 2025, not number of cars.
fieldNotes.rejectionPct: Hylkäys-%: share of periodic inspections that ended in rejection (hylätty). Traficom value; 2 decimals in the xlsx rows, 1 decimal in PxWeb-based blocks.
fieldNotes.rejected: Hylätyt: number of rejected inspections (from PxWeb).
fieldNotes.avgKm / medianKm: Odometer reading at inspection (ajettujen kilometrien keskiarvo / mediaani), rounded by Traficom to 1000 km.
fieldNotes.topRejectionCauses: Traficom's three most common rejection causes for the row, in Traficom's order (area = Finnish fault object name). rejectionFaults = number of rejection-causing faults found on that object (PxWeb 050), per100Inspections = rejectionFaults / inspections * 100 (our calculation). A single inspection can have several faults, so per100 is not exactly the % of cars. Empty list = Traficom published no cause for that row; it does not mean that no fault was common. Corrected 2026-10-17: an earlier version said no fault object reached 10 rejection faults in any empty row. That is wrong for 6 of the 272 empty byModel rows, all first registered 2021 (Kia RIO, Toyota COROLLA, Toyota RAV4, Volkswagen GOLF, Volvo XC40, Volvo XC60). Example: Toyota COROLLA 2021 has 34 tyre-and-rim rejection faults in 5,118 inspections in PxWeb 050. See notes for Traficom's inclusion rule.
fieldNotes.areaEn / mainAreaEn / powertrain: English labels are our own translations, not official Traficom wording. Hints in brackets, such as '(rust)' in 'Underbody box sections and floor panel (rust)' or '(control arms, ball joints, bushings)', are our interpretation of the typical fault; Traficom's names do not contain them.
fieldNotes.sharePct (commonFaults): Share of all rejection-causing faults found in 2025 in cars first registered 2005-2021 (our calculation from PxWeb 050).
fieldNotes.averageByAge vs averageByVehicleAge: averageByAge = all makes/models by first registration year, same base as byModel (use it to compare a model with the average). averageByVehicleAge = every passenger car inspection in 2025 by exact age class (PxWeb 030). The two age definitions are not the same: PxWeb 030 age class 4 has 107,200 inspections in 2025, while first registration year 2021 in the xlsx has 104,458. Compare a model row with averageByAge, not with averageByVehicleAge.

notes: Model rows exist only for model series with at least 100 periodic inspections in 2025 (per first registration year); cars 4-20 years old (first registration 2005-2021). Source: PxWeb table note and tieto.traficom.fi/fi/tilastot/katsastustilasto.
Traficom: rejection percentages of different models are not directly comparable because average mileage differs a lot between models; compare avgKm/medianKm too.

Traficom publishes at most three rejection causes per row. Its statistics page (tieto.traficom.fi/fi/tilastot/katsastustilasto, updated 6.5.2026) says a fault is included if it was found at least ten times for the model series, or if its rejection faults were at least 1% of the series' inspections in the year ('vähintään kymmenen tai ... vähintään yksi prosentti'). The published 2025 lists follow neither reading exactly: tested against PxWeb 050 on 2026-10-17, 'at least 10 AND at least 1%' reproduces 3,015 of 3,315 rows and 'at least 10 OR at least 1%' reproduces 2,537, and causes tied at the cut-off are sometimes left out. If the app derives causes for rows Traficom left empty, label them as derived from PxWeb 050, not as Traficom's top causes. Traficom's cause order agreed with the PxWeb fault counts in all 2,964 rows that have causes.

Rejection percentages in the xlsx (2 decimals) and PxWeb (1 decimal) differ in 173 rows only by double rounding (e.g. 48.45 vs 48.4); every row's rejectionPct equals rejected / inspections * 100 to 2 decimals.
Model series names are Traficom's (models merged into series, e.g. "BMW 3-sarja"); matching against an ad title needs make + model-series normalisation (case-insensitive, e.g. "Golf" -> "GOLF").

Model statistics cover only cars first registered 2005-2021 (ages 4-20). Most cars first registered in 2022 or later were not yet due for their first periodic inspection in 2025 (due within 4 years of first use), so there are no model rows for them. Some younger cars are inspected anyway: taxis must be inspected yearly (VNa 1455/2019, 3 §), and PxWeb 030 lists 12,172 passenger car inspections in age classes 0-3 in 2025.
Inspection schedule rule changes (2018, 2020) affect which ages are inspected in a given year (see averageByVehicleAge counts).

factCheck.method: Independent re-download and re-parse of the Traficom xlsx; fresh PxWeb API queries (tables 030, 040, 050); Traficom news of 6.5.2026, statistics page and inspection-schedule page; Katsastusalan tilannekatsaus 2025 PDF; Finlex VNa 1455/2019.
verified: All 3,315 xlsx rows (byModel, byMake, averageByAge, byModelAllYears, byMakeAllYears, national.ages4to20): inspections, rejection %, average and median km and cause names match the xlsx exactly.
national, nationalByYear, averageByVehicleAge, byPowertrainAndAge and byPowertrainByYear match PxWeb 030 exactly (cells Traficom shows as '.' are null here).

rejected counts match PxWeb 040 in the rows spot-checked (national 449,267; Volkswagen GOLF, Tesla MODEL 3 and MODEL Y, Toyota COROLLA, Skoda OCTAVIA for 2015, 2018 and 2021) and agree with rejectionPct in every row.

Every rejectionFaults value in topRejectionCauses (all blocks), commonFaults, commonFaultsByMainArea and commonFaultsByFirstRegYear matches PxWeb 050 exactly; front axle 126,260 = 16.12% of 783,266 rejection faults.

Press release figures (over 2.18 million; 30% vs 29%; EV inspections 31,432 vs 15,513; EV rejection 23% vs 20%; age 4: EV 19.6%, petrol 5.4%, diesel 10.8%; EV age 4 in 2024 16.1%) match the Traficom news page of 6.5.2026.
Inspection prices (Taulukko 3) and the 2025 supervision figures (148 cars; 95 = 64.2%; 7 = 4.7%; 107 = 72.3%) match the PDF.
The inspection schedule matches the Traficom page and VNa 1455/2019, 3 § and 4 §.
corrections: fieldNotes.topRejectionCauses: removed the false claim that no empty-cause row has a fault object with 10 or more rejection faults (6 rows do).
notes: Traficom's cause inclusion rule is now quoted correctly ('at least 10 or at least 1%'), with the finding that the published lists follow neither reading exactly.
notes: the claim that cars first registered 2022 or later had no periodic inspection in 2025 was softened (taxis are inspected yearly; PxWeb 030 has 12,172 inspections at ages 0-3).
inspectionQualityCheck: '22 cars = 14.0%' is printed in the source but 22/148 = 14.9%; flagged as inconsistent.
inspectionSchedule: added the 8-9-year transition rule, the 'passed within 30 days' wording, the taxi exception and the Finlex legal source.
inspectionPrices: only the 2025 figure is stated as spring 2025; the vehicle class is not named in the table (assumption marked as estimate).
notChecked: Licence and reuse terms of the Traficom data: the statistics page shows only '© Traficom' and names no open licence.
Whether the inspection prices include VAT (still an assumption).

national.scope: All passenger car periodic inspections in Finland in 2025, all ages and powertrains.

ages4to20.scope: Cars first registered 2005-2021, all makes and models (model-statistics base).

topRejectionCauses.areaEn: Front axle (control arms, ball joints, bushings)

pressRelease.commonFaultsNote: Front axle faults are the most common cause of rejections and repair orders, over ten per hundred inspections; for 4-year-old EVs the most common rejection faults were play in rear-axle trailing/upper control arm joints and in front lower control arm ball joints.

inspectionSchedule.vehicleClass: Passenger car (henkilöauto, M1) not used as a taxi. Taxis are inspected yearly from first use (VNa 1455/2019, 3 § 1 mom. 2 kohta).
inspectionSchedule.firstInspection: No later than 4 years after the date the car was first taken into use (käyttöönottopäivä).
inspectionSchedule.thenEvery: No later than 2 years after the previous inspection, until more than 10 years have passed since first use (see transition).
inspectionSchedule.annuallyFrom: Every year (no later than 1 year after the previous inspection) once more than 10 years have passed since first use.
inspectionSchedule.transition: Traficom: if the car is inspected 8-9 years after first use (e.g. at 8 y 5 mo), the next inspection is still due by age 10 y 0 mo; if it is inspected more than 9 years after first use, the next one is due within 1 year.
inspectionSchedule.sameDueDateWindow: The next due date does not change if the car is inspected and passed on the last day of its inspection window or in the 30 days before it (VNa 1455/2019, 4 § 2 mom.: 'hyväksytty ... enintään 30 vuorokautta ennen'). A car passed earlier gets a new due date counted from that inspection. Traficom example: window ends 19.11.2024; passed 20.10.-19.11.2024 keeps 19.11.2025 as the next date; passed 10.8.2024 moves it to 10.8.2025.
inspectionSchedule.oldVehicles: Privately used vehicles: every 2 years once the previous inspection was done after 40 years had passed from the end of the first-use year (VNa 1455/2019, 3 § 1 mom. 8 kohta; in force 14.5.2020).
inspectionSchedule.howToCheck: Due date shown in Traficom Oma asiointi, on the inspection certificate, or in part I of the registration certificate.
inspectionSchedule.note: Checked 2026-10-17 against the Traficom page (updated 10.2.2026) and the consolidated text of Valtioneuvoston asetus ajoneuvojen liikennekelpoisuuden valvonnasta 1455/2019 (3 § and 4 §, in force 14.5.2020) on Finlex. English wording is our paraphrase.

inspectionPrices.what: Average prices in euros of periodic inspection services, from inspection station price lists (Taulukko 3, Katsastusalan tilannekatsaus 2025). The report gives the 2025 walk-in average as of spring 2025. Walk-in prices (ilman ajanvarausta) unless "Booked". Table 3 does not name the vehicle class; we assume passenger car prices (estimate).
notes: Traficom: the 2024 package prices are not comparable with 2023 because the price collection method changed and earlier data had errors in the packages with emissions measurement.
Traficom: EV inspection pricing usually follows the periodic inspection + emissions test package.
"Booked" = with advance booking (ennakkovaraus). reInspection = jälkitarkastus after a rejection.
The table does not say whether VAT is included; they are station list prices, so consumer prices incl. VAT are assumed (estimate).

missedAtLeastThreeSeriousFaults.note: Both values as printed in the source (section 4.2: '22 katsastuksessa (14,0 % kaikista uudelleentarkastuksista)'). But 22/148 = 14.9%, so the source's count and percentage disagree; one of them is probably a typo. Do not show this figure without that caveat.

inspectionQualityCheck.caveat: Traficom re-inspected these cars right after a periodic inspection as supervision; supervision is targeted risk-based at stations, so this is not a random sample of all inspections.
